title: Become an ambassador
description: The Labs in three minutes, five questions, the ambassador agreement, and your name. About ten minutes.
privacy: Until sign-in is ready, this stays on your device. You'll share it with your coordinator at the end.

you.title: Your name.
you.lede: So your coordinator knows who's in.
you.referredByHint: If an ambassador or Mentor sent you, their name counts toward their pin.

errors.email: Add an email address like name@example.com.

agreement.title: The ambassador agreement.

sections.p: You and The Upskilling Labs. You're volunteering as an ambassador: you're not staff, and there's no pay.
Have real conversations with people you know, tell your own story, and invite them to one dated next step. When you're ready, give one short talk to a room. Bring someone new along.

Use the guide's words. Describe our legal status exactly as the guide says it. Never promise jobs, pay, or outcomes, and never speak for The Labs to the press or officials without asking your coordinator first.
You don't collect anyone's contact details for The Labs. People Join The Labs themselves at theupskillinglabs.org.
Our Code of Conduct applies to ambassadors everywhere you represent The Labs, online and in person.
You can stop any time. Tell your coordinator, and you're always welcome back. If an ambassador breaks this agreement or the Code of Conduct, we may ask them to step back.
This is a plain-language summary. The Upskilling Labs' Terms of Service, Privacy Policy, and Code of Conduct govern in full.

agreement.check: I agree to the Ambassador Agreement and the Code of Conduct.
agreement.error: Tick the box to agree before you continue.

video.title: The Labs in three minutes.
video.lede: Watch it, or read the short version. The five questions come from this.
read: Nobody finds The Labs from an ad. They find it because someone they know said “come with me.”
The Labs is free. Workshops, Build Cycles, all of it. Run by volunteers. Born at DC Public Library in fall 2025.
People pick the problems. Small teams build real things. Everyone teaches what they learn.
Your job is three moves. Ask what they're working toward. Share thirty seconds of your story. Invite them to one dated next step.
You never sell, sign anyone up, or promise a job. People Join The Labs themselves at theupskillinglabs.org.
If anyone asks what we are: “a fiscally sponsored project of Superbloom Design, a 501(c)(3). Our own status is pending.”

quiz.title: The five questions everyone asks.
quiz.lede: You'll hear these in every conversation. Four of five and you're set. Try as often as you like.
quiz.passed: You passed. You can answer what people actually ask, and that's most of the job.
quiz.failed: Not yet. Look again at the ones marked, then try again.

questions.q: What does it cost to take part in The Labs?
questions.why: The Labs is free: workshops and Build Cycles cost nothing.

questions.q: Someone asks, “Is this like a coding bootcamp?” What do you say?
options: Not really. There's no curriculum. You work with a small team on a real problem and learn what you need along the way.
It's all online, at your own pace.
questions.why: No curriculum to get through. A small team, a real problem, and you learn what you need on the way.

questions.q: In a Build Cycle, who chooses the problems The Labs takes on?
options: The participants, and everyone gets a vote
questions.why: Participants choose the problems. Everyone gets a vote.

questions.q: You meet someone who might like The Labs. What's your job?
options: Get their phone number for the coordinator
Sign them in on your phone
Ask what they're working toward, share your story, and invite them to one dated next step
Send them a list of every event
questions.why: Ask, share, invite. You don't collect contact details: people Join The Labs themselves.

questions.q: Someone asks whether The Labs is a nonprofit. What do you say?
options: "A fiscally sponsored project of Superbloom Design, a 501(c)(3). Our own status is pending."
